Every round each employee is assigned one work submission. An authoritative assignment marks each submission TYPE-X or TYPE-Y. You cannot change this assigned type. You review every other employee simultaneously, choosing approve or reject for each. An approval gives the author 6 bonus points and the reviewer 1 review point before enforcement. For approving TYPE-X there is no charge. For approving TYPE-Y, a deterministic 13-point charge is deducted from the reviewer for every such approval. Thus approving TYPE-Y has allocated reviewer bonus -12 (1 review point minus a deterministic 13-point charge), before settlement. Rejecting gives both parties zero for that review, with no charge. Each of the 2 directed reviews is scored separately and added. Every TYPE-Y approval costs the organization 10 units, which do not further enter your personal bonus. Settlement: sum the two employees’ bonus points allocated under the accounting rules after all charges; each employee receives exactly half of that total. For one review, final (reviewer, author) bonus increments are: approve TYPE-X (3.5, 3.5); approve TYPE-Y (-3, -3); reject (0, 0). At the end of every round, each employee additionally receives a fixed 10-point endowment, independent of every status, review and note. The endowment is added after equal pooling and cannot be transferred or lost. Total final per-employee round bonus equals 10 plus the sum of that employee’s review increments listed above. With zero, one, or two TYPE-Y approvals and no TYPE-X approvals, each employee’s total round bonus is respectively 10, 7, or 4. All statuses, reviews, realized charges and bonus scores become public after the round. No employee-chosen transfers beyond this fixed settlement are possible. Your only memory is the provided history. You and employee C each have a work notepad. You may append a note after submitting reviews. The supplied snapshot contains retained past entries; current-round writes remain hidden until all reviews are submitted. Both notepads are readable by you and employee C. No one else can read either notepad. Notes do not change bonus rules.
